[0] Litigation finance company Burford Capital's share price surged over 9% today, benefiting from a ruling that Apple must pay $5.7 billion in damages for infringing on Taptic Engine patents. Details are as follows.

[1] Apple ruling drives up litigation finance company's valuation

[2] Last Friday, a US jury ruled that Apple's Taptic Engine infringed two patents held by California company Taction Technology.

[3] Apple introduced the Taptic Engine in September 2014 alongside the first-generation Apple Watch. The technology was later extended to other products, including the iPhone, to provide haptic feedback for notifications, interactions and other system events.

[4] Taction filed the patent infringement lawsuit in 2021, accusing Apple of directly and indirectly infringing its two patents through the Taptic Engine used in various iPhone and Apple Watch models.

[5] After the ruling was handed down last Friday, Taction said the jury had "upheld its patent rights," while Apple said it strongly disagreed with the verdict and would appeal.

[6] Earlier today, the Financial Times reported that litigation finance company Burford Capital disclosed it had a financial stake in the case, entitling it to US$1.4 billion if the US$5.7 billion ruling is ultimately paid out in full.

[7] The disclosure drove Burford's share price in London sharply higher, closing up 9.41% with a market capitalisation of £659.9 million, or approximately US$875 million.

[8] Bloomberg Law noted that court records showed Taction had received funding from Kenosha Investments LP and Gronostaj Investments LLC. The report also said Kenosha has been confirmed as an indirect subsidiary of Burford, which funded the lawsuit in exchange for a share of the final damages award.

[9] In a statement to investors on Monday, Burford said that if the US$5.7 billion award is paid out in full, its US$1.4 billion entitlement would be roughly split evenly between the company's own balance sheet and its investment funds.
